Copying the comment I left on the video:

Interesting discussion. I think GamerGate should end at some point and while we've had a lot of great victories, there's still a lot of work to be done. I think a larger social justice pushback is needed in society, but that GamerGate should focus primarily on corruption and censorship in gaming. Criticism of social justice outside of the gaming industry is a related, but largely separate topic that should betackled as such and mostly kept off the hashtag.

I also think that Undertow has a very skewed view of NotYourShield and the evolution of GamerGate. I'm not sure where you're looking if you think that GamerGate has become "virtue signaling" about "how great anti-SJW minorities and LGBT people are." It's great to see people telling the media and social justice crybullies that they don't speak on behalf of women, minorities or LGB people. Women, minorities and LGBT people can speak for themselves and no single ideology represents them.

As for Milo being "worshipped" by GamerGate, that's nonsense. He has some fanboys, but most of us recognize that he's in it for himself. If he does something unethical, we'll call him out on it and many disagree with some of his non-GamerGate views. Some people like him and some don't, just like Sargon or Internet Aristocrat or Andredal or Appabend or Mombot or Christina Hoff Sommers or any other Youtuber or popular figure.

Internet Aristocrat's "attack attack attack" theory was vague and effectively meaningless. Long since IA flamed out, GamerGate has and continues to stand against the social justice crowd. What more could you possibly want? If you want us to start doxing people and adopting SJW tactics, then you're going to become no better than them. Undertow, you are admittedly far-right and that's fine, but GamerGate wasn't and isn't your personal army.

On GamerGate being too "PR" friendly, I think you're missing the point. Very few people honestly care about "PR" in the sense of getting the media to like us. The GamerGate community doesn't support becoming the extremists that we are fighting, that isn't "PR," that's having values and being consistent. We should focus on being ourselves and letting our image speak for itself, and to a degree, care about PR among fellow gamers. If a journalist wants to write an honest artile about GamerGate, then that's great and we would be willing to work with them, but we certainly aren't trying to suck up to them for "good PR."

On the discussion of "walking simulators," I think it's fine to criticize them and the direction you feel the industry is taking, but they are hardly the only games being made. I think it would be great to have more niche and diverse games out there, and walking simulators are a part of that. If people want to make and play walking simulators or games like The Walking Dead or Life is Strange (which imho was a fantastic game), then more power to them. And touching upon the discussion around 35:00, SJWs should be able to make their own games, as long as they don't try to gatekeep and police what other people want to create.

The discussion on morality and choices in games is pretty interesting. Denying people the ability to make "bad" choices is an often overlooked core belief of the social justice warriors. This has become much more apparent lately with people like Jonathan McIntosh and Bob Chipman effectively saying as much about player choice in games. Even if a choice were objectively morally wrong, it's still just a video game and people should be allowed to make those choices.

As for what GamerGate has accomplished, you need only look at the regressive left's strength from a year or two ago and compare it to today. We took a group that hailed themselves as untouchable and above criticism, and we exposed them as the authoritarians, hypocrites and hacks that they are. We likely aren't going to see much in the way of major campaigns from the regressives to censor games like we saw in 2014 and 2015. And that's not even touching upon the ethics victories.
